headings.title: Meaning of owner for sections 242.010 to 242.690
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12364, A.L. 2002 S.B. 941; prior revisions 1929 § 10783, 1919 § 4415). Defines 'owner' as the deed-record freehold estate owner for sections 242.010 to 242.690, excludes reversioners, remaindermen, trustees, and mortgagees from counting, publication notice, and process, and provides representation by present freehold owners. Source note cites 1953 Farmers Drainage Dist. v. Sinclair Refining Co. holding a corporate easement holder to be an owner entitled to notice under §§ 242.020 and 242.030.

headings.title: Entity delegation of representation and voting rights
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Covers permissive ('may') delegation by corporations, partnerships, joint ventures, or other non-individual property owners of an individual representative for public votes and before the board of supervisors, treated as owner with statutory benefits and privileges including board service if elected.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections) and all source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12364, A.L. 2002 S.B. 941; prior revisions 1929–1919); verified sourceUrl, sourceSha256, textSha256, numbering, and both bodySha256 fingerprints. Checked section-range scope (242.010 to 242.690), excluded interest holders and freehold-owner representation in (1), permissive entity delegation and board-service privileges in (2), and the 1953 Farmers Drainage Dist. v. Sinclair Refining Co. (255 S.W.2d 745) easement-owner notice annotation. Retained both titles as accurate and concise.

headings.title: District formation authority and articles of association
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12324; prior revisions 1929–1909). Covers majority-acreage owners of contiguous swamp, wet, or overflowed lands forming a drainage district for enumerated sanitary, agricultural, public health/welfare, or utility purposes, and required contents of articles of association including name, duration, boundaries, owners/property descriptions, unknown-owner statements, tax obligation, and prayer under sections 242.010 to 242.690. Source note cites 1953 Farmers Drainage Dist. v. Sinclair Refining Co. regarding omitting a corporate easement description.

headings.title: Filing signed articles with circuit clerk
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires signed articles of association and petition to be filed with the circuit clerk of the county where the lands and property lie, or the county containing the largest portion when tracts span two or more counties.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections) and all source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12324; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and both subsection fingerprints. Checked majority-acreage formation purposes, required articles contents and tax-obligation recital under sections 242.010 to 242.690 in (1), single- and multi-county circuit clerk filing venue in (2), and the 1953 Farmers Drainage Dist. v. Sinclair Refining Co. (255 S.W.2d 745) annotation on omitted corporate easements (retaining exact archived annotation text). Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Publication requirements and notice form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including the statutory form table ('NOTICE OF APPLICATION TO FORM DRAINAGE DISTRICT') and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12325, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, effective 1-2-79). Covers circuit clerk publication once a week for four consecutive weeks in each county with district property, with last insertion at least 15 days before the next regular court term, and prescribes a substantially sufficient form for sections 242.010 to 242.690.

headings.title: Circuit court jurisdiction and multicounty notices
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Grants original and exclusive jurisdiction coextensive with district boundaries regardless of county lines to the filing county's circuit court for sections 242.010 to 242.690, subject to the proviso that multicounty notices need list only property located in each respective county.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections, including the embedded statutory form table in (1)) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12325, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, effective 1-2-79); verified source identity and both subsection fingerprints. Checked four-week publication timing (last insertion at least 15 days before next regular term), notice form table referencing chapter 242 in (1), and exclusive coextensive circuit court jurisdiction with the multicounty property-listing proviso in (2). Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Filing objections, summary hearing, decree, or dismissal
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12326; prior revisions 1929–1909). Covers non-signing owners filing objections on or before the first day of term limited to denying articles statements, summary hearing, incorporation decree for a term not exceeding the articles if overruled, or dismissal with costs adjudged proportionally by acreage against signers.

headings.title: Signer dismissal restrictions and amending articles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Prohibits a signer of the articles of association from dismissing proceedings as to that signer without written consent of a majority in acreage of signing owners, and allows amending articles like any other pleading.

headings.title: Filing incorporation decree with secretary of state
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs the circuit clerk within 60 days after incorporation to transmit a certified copy of findings and decree to the secretary of state for filing like general corporate articles.

headings.title: Recording decree and plat with county recorders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires filing a copy of the findings, decree, and district plat as a permanent record with each affected county recorder, setting a one-dollar filing and preservation fee.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12326; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and all four subsection fingerprints. Checked non-signing owner objection timing and scope, summary hearing, decree vs. dismissal with proportional signer costs in (1), signer dismissal consent bar and pleading-style amendments in (2), 60-day secretary of state filing in (3), and county recorder permanent filing ($1 fee) in (4). Revised (1) to include dismissal alongside decree for neutrality and (2) to 'Signer dismissal restrictions and amending articles' to match statutory terms; retained (3) and (4).

headings.title: Petition to annex adjacent or common-outlet lands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12365; prior revisions 1929 § 10784, 1919 § 4416). Authorizes the board of supervisors or majority-acreage owners of adjacent or common-outlet wet/overflow lands to petition the organizing court clerk to extend boundaries, and sets required boundary, owner, tract-description, and unknown-owner contents.

headings.title: Published notice of annexation petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires four consecutive weekly newspaper publications in each county containing lands sought to be annexed, allows section/part-section descriptions without owner names, and specifies notice statements on purpose, tax liability, and the 15-day post-publication objection deadline.

headings.title: Objections, speedy hearing, and annexation order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Grants non-petitioning owners or a non-petitioning board 15 days after last publication to file objections limited to denying petition statements, directs speedy hearing at a regular, adjourned, or special term, and mandates annexing qualifying wet, overflow, or common-outlet lands.

headings.title: Reclaiming enlarged district and amending plans
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Directs the board of supervisors after extension to reclaim enlarged district property by executing or completing existing or future reclamation plans or adopting enlargements, additions, and extensions, proceeding as nearly as possible under sections 242.010 to 242.690.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence and meaning of lying adjacent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Makes petitions, chief engineer maps, profiles, and reports, and board records prima facie evidence in section proceedings, and defines how courts must construe 'lying adjacent to the district'.

headings.title: Appeals from annexation findings or decrees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Grants any owner of lands or other property, or the board of supervisors on the district's behalf, a right to appeal an order extending or refusing to extend district boundaries under the civil code.

headings.title: Remedial construction and applicability of amendments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Declares the section's amendments remedial, requires prompt liberal judicial construction, and applies them to districts already organized, in process of organization, or thereafter organized by Missouri circuit courts.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (7 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12365; prior revisions 1929–1919); verified source identity and all seven subsection fingerprints. Checked petition standing and contents in (1), four-week published notice with 15-day objection deadline in (2), non-petitioning owner/board objections and speedy hearing at regular/adjourned/special term in (3), enlarged-district reclamation in (4), prima facie evidence and statutory construction of 'lying adjacent to the district' in (5), civil-code appeals in (6), and remedial construction and applicability in (7). Revised (3) from 'summary hearing' to 'speedy hearing' to match statutory phrasing ('as early and speedily as possible'); retained (1), (2), and (4)–(7).

headings.title: Authority to consolidate adjacent districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12372, A.L. 1959 H.B. 312; prior revisions 1929–1909; cross-reference to 243.450). Authorizes uniting two or more adjacent districts in the same or different counties into one district with the rights, powers, and privileges of districts under sections 242.010 to 242.690.

headings.title: Consolidation elections and circuit court petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires each original board to call an election like supervisor elections and, upon majority approval of acreage voting in each district, to petition the circuit court of the county with the greatest land area with election returns and specified district details.

headings.title: Notice of consolidation petition under section 242.030
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs the circuit clerk upon petition filing to give notice in the manner of section 242.030 stating petition contents, objects sought, and the hearing date.

headings.title: Objections, consolidation order, recording, and prior bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Covers landowner objections by the hearing date, court consolidation order and section 242.010 to 242.690 powers, assumption of original liens/liabilities, election of a new board, recording certified orders with county recorders ($1 fee) and secretary of state, and the proviso keeping taxes for pre-existing outstanding bonds an obligation only of property within the issuing component district.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12372, A.L. 1959 H.B. 312; prior revisions 1929–1909; cross-reference to 243.450); verified source identity and all four subsection fingerprints. Checked consolidation authority under sections 242.010 to 242.690 in (1), majority-acreage-voting elections and greatest-land-area circuit court petition in (2), section 242.030 notice in (3), and objections, consolidation order, new board election, recording ($1 fee), and the component-district pre-existing bond tax proviso in (4). Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Eligibility of existing districts to reorganize
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12380; prior revisions 1929 § 10799, 1919 § 4429). Authorizes drainage districts previously organized, in process of organization, or thereafter organized under any previous or existing state law to organize under sections 242.010 to 242.690 and receive their benefits.

headings.title: Articles of association for reorganization
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Permits majority-acreage owners of an existing district to sign articles stating the unchanged district name, duration not shorter than existing obligations, unchanged boundaries, existing land/owner records, and a petition for declaration under sections 242.010 to 242.690.

headings.title: Filing reorganization articles with circuit clerk
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires signed reorganization articles to be filed with the circuit clerk of the county where the lands lie, or the county containing the largest share of lands if multi-county.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12380; prior revisions 1929–1919); verified source identity and all three subsection fingerprints. Checked reorganization eligibility for prior, pending, and future districts under sections 242.010 to 242.690 in (1), majority-acreage articles preserving name, boundaries, records, and obligation-life duration in (2), and single- or multi-county circuit clerk filing in (3). Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Calling landowner meeting to extend corporate existence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12373; prior revisions 1929 § 10792, 1919 § 4422). Applies to districts under sections 242.010 to 242.690 or prior circuit-court drainage acts when the board finds extension necessary for listed financial/construction reasons or other cause, requiring a meeting called under section 242.150 with notice of time, place, purpose, and court-petition consequence of majority-acreage approval.

headings.title: Meeting conduct, petition filing, and court procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs conducting the meeting under section 242.150 with a supervisor as chairman and board secretary or deputy as clerk, filing a circuit court petition within 45 days before the next term upon majority-acreage vote, and following sections 242.030 and 242.040 procedures.

headings.title: Filing extension decree or dismissing petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires transmitting a granted decree within 20 days to the board secretary for filing with the secretary of state and each affected county recorder ($1 fee), or dismissing the petition with costs paid by the district if denied.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12373; prior revisions 1929–1919); verified source identity and all three subsection fingerprints. Checked applicability to sections 242.010 to 242.690 and prior circuit-court drainage acts with section 242.150 meeting notice in (1), meeting officers, 45-day court petition, and sections 242.030/242.040 procedure in (2), and 20-day decree transmission, secretary of state and county recorder ($1 fee) filings, or dismissal at district cost in (3). Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Pre-bond dissolution, accounting, surplus, and deficiency tax
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12361, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, effective 1-2-79; prior revision 1929 § 10780). Mandates dissolution upon majority-acreage petition before bonds are issued and negotiated, subject to court accounting of treasury funds versus unpaid warrants/debts, immediate payment and proportional refund of excess, or a uniform per-acre tax levy to cover any deficiency. Source note cites 1980 Matter of Little Chariton Drainage Dist. on court authority to order additional levies for dissolution debts.

headings.title: Calling dissolution meeting, notice, and annual limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Allows the board—and requires it upon petition of one-tenth of landowners owning one-tenth of lands—to call a dissolution meeting once all bonds and debts are paid or funds suffice for debts and dissolution costs, with three successive weeks' newspaper notice and a limit of one dissolution meeting per year.

headings.title: Dissolution petition and published show-cause notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs the board, upon approval by a majority of voting landowners owning a majority of voting acreage, to file a circuit court petition reciting bond, debt, and cost-funding facts, and provides four successive weeks' newspaper show-cause notice at least 15 days before return day. Retains archived phrasing 'that due notice has been given or the clerk thereof in vacation shall cause notice to be given' without alteration.

headings.title: Dissolution hearing, debt payment, surplus, and bridge condition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Covers court findings and dissolution order (either immediately when no debts remain or after ordered debt payment is shown), distribution of excess funds, and the proviso that dissolution is not effective until drainage-ditch bridges are sufficient and in reasonable repair.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and all source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12361, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, effective 1-2-79; prior revision 1929 § 10780; 1980 Matter of Little Chariton Drainage Dist., 602 S.W.2d 916, on court authority to order additional levies for dissolution debts); verified source identity and all four subsection fingerprints. Tightened (1) to 'Pre-bond dissolution, accounting, surplus, and deficiency tax'; retained (2)–(4).

headings.title: Drainage works, bridges, roadways, and property acquisition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12349, A.L. 1969 H.B. 53; prior revisions 1929–1909; cross-references 70.377, 409.950, 369.194). Empowers the board inside or outside the district to alter/clean/divert waterways, build/maintain drainage works, bridges, and levee roadways, cross public highways and railroads, remove structures, and acquire or condemn property, easements, or materials. Retains archived source spelling 'tract' alongside 'track'.

headings.title: Water power, hydroelectric plants, and surplus power leases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Authorizes the board to control water power created by district works, build and maintain hydroelectric plants using unappropriated district treasury funds, and lease surplus power with lease proceeds deposited in the district treasury.

headings.title: Condemnation of unacquired property and procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Authorizes the board to condemn land or property inside or outside the district not acquired on the commissioners' benefits-and-damages report, using statutory appropriation procedures for telegraph, telephone, and railroad rights-of-way.

headings.title: Permitted investments for funds not immediately needed
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and cross-reference notes (70.377, 409.950, 369.194). Permits investing funds not immediately needed for operating expenses in (1) U.S. direct or guaranteed obligations, (2) accounts of savings and loan associations insured by the Federal Savings and Loan Insurance Corporation (archived agency reference retained), and (3) bank savings accounts and time deposits/CDs.

headings.title: Election of board president and secretary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12330, A.L. 1983 H.B. 236, A.L. 2002 S.B. 941; prior revisions 1929–1909). Directs the board immediately after election to choose one member as president and elect a secretary serving until a successor qualifies, who must reside in a district county or adjoining county and need not be a board member.

headings.title: Official seal and open record of proceedings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires adopting an official seal and keeping a record of all board proceedings open to inspection by district real estate and property owners and all other interested parties.

headings.title: Annual work report to landowners under section 242.160
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires the board to report work performed by engineers or otherwise to landowners at the annual meeting held under section 242.160.

headings.title: Setting board compensation at annual meeting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Provides that compensation for board members' services while actually engaged in district work is determined at the annual meeting held under section 242.160.

Checked board president selection and secretary residency/eligibility in (1), seal and open proceedings record in (2), annual work report at the section 242.160 meeting in (3), and setting board compensation for actual district work at that annual meeting in (4). headings.title: Secretary serving as treasurer and receiving revenues
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12348, A.L. 1969 H.B. 53, A.L. 2002 S.B. 941; prior revisions 1929–1909). Makes the board secretary the district treasurer except as otherwise provided, tasked with receiving and receipting drainage taxes from county collectors and tax sale proceeds under sections 242.010 to 242.690.

headings.title: Treasurer compensation, office, equipment, and records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Covers monthly salary fixed by the board, necessary expenses, board-furnished office room and listed supplies/equipment in a district or adjoining county, and keeping district records in that office.

headings.title: Appointment and pay of deputy treasurers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Permits the treasurer, with board advice and consent, to appoint one or more necessary deputies whose salaries and necessary expenses are paid by the district.

headings.title: Treasurer official bond and custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires a treasurer's bond fixed and approved by the board (at least two sureties, or a surety/bonding company if directed) in addition to the section 242.480 bond-proceeds bond, covering tax and other receipts, and kept by the board president separately from secretary-treasurer papers.

headings.title: Depositing district funds and crediting interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires depositing all received funds in board-designated bank(s) or trust company and crediting all paid interest to the district.

headings.title: Annual audit, financial report, publication, and filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Requires the board to audit or have audited the treasurer's books annually, report at the annual landowner meeting, publish a receipt/disbursement/balance statement within 30 days, and file a copy with each affected county clerk.

headings.title: Paying funds by warrant and statutory warrant form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 including the statutory warrant form table and notes. Restricts treasury payouts to district warrants signed by the board president and attested by the secretary-treasurer, and prescribes the warrant form.

headings.title: Appointing chief engineer, assistants, and consultants
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12331; prior revisions 1929–1909). Requires appointing a chief engineer (individual, copartnership, or corporation) within 60 days of organizing to control district engineering work with board-approved assistants and permissive board-consented consultation of eminent engineers.

headings.title: Surveys, written reclamation report, maps, and profiles
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs the engineer(s) to survey district and adjacent benefitted lands and submit a written reclamation plan report with maps and profiles depicting physical land characteristics, public roads, railroads, rights-of-way, and improvements.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12331; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and both subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Filing reclamation plan and petitioning for commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12334, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070; prior revisions 1929–1909). Requires the board secretary within 20 days after plan adoption to transmit a certified copy to the organizing circuit clerk while the board petitions for appointment of commissioners to appraise property and assess benefits and damages.

headings.title: Appointment, qualifications, and quorum of commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs the court within 30 days after petition filing to appoint three Missouri-resident commissioners who neither own district land nor are kin within the fourth degree of consanguinity to a district landowner, and sets a majority quorum controlling board action.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12334, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, A.L. 1990 H.B. 1070; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and both subsection fingerprints. Checked 20-day certified plan transmission and petition for appraisal/assessment commissioners in (1), and 30-day court appointment of three non-landowner, non-fourth-degree-kin Missouri-resident commissioners with majority quorum control in (2). Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Clerk notice of appointment and first meeting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12335; prior revisions 1929–1909). Directs the circuit clerk upon filing the appointment order to notify each commissioner in writing or print with the time and place of the first meeting.

headings.title: Meeting attendance and documents furnished by secretary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires the board secretary or deputy to attend the first meeting and provide a complete list of affected district and adjacent lands/corporate/other property and owner names from the articles at decree date, plus the reclamation plan, maps, and profiles.

headings.title: Commissioners' oath, chairman election, and ex officio secretary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires commissioners to take and subscribe an impartiality oath at the meeting or within 10 days, elect one member as chairman, and designates the board secretary or deputy as ex officio secretary of the commissioners.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12335; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and all three subsection fingerprints. Revised (2) to 'Meeting attendance and documents furnished by secretary' to cover attendance as well as documents; retained (1) and (3).

headings.title: Starting duties, legal advice, and engineering assistance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12336, A.L. 1985 H.B. 378; prior revisions 1929–1909). Directs commissioners to begin duties within 30 days after qualifying under section 242.250, allows requesting legal advice from the attorney of the district, and requires the chief engineer or an assistant to accompany them and give written opinions on request.

headings.title: Viewing premises and assessing values, benefits, and damages
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs commissioners to view premises, value property to be acquired inside or outside the district for plan works, and assess benefits and damages accruing to lots/tracts, public highways, railroads, rights-of-way, and other property.

headings.title: Benefit assessment limits, credits, roadways, and plan restriction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Limits benefits on non-traversed property to works in the adopted plan or drainage/overflow protection provided, requires crediting existing drains or levees, sets increased physical efficiency and decreased maintenance cost as the measure for highways/railroads/roadways, and bars commissioners from altering the plan.

headings.title: Required tabular format and columns of report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires arranging the commissioners' findings in tabular form with seven specifically titled columns covering owner, description, acres assessed, benefits assessed, right-of-way acres taken, value taken, and damages.

headings.title: Cost estimates, tabulation, signatures, and court filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires commissioners with engineer advice to estimate and tabulate plan works costs including property/damages and board-estimated organization/administration expenses, with a majority signing and filing the report with the organizing circuit clerk.

headings.title: Clerical assistance and report preparation by secretary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Requires the board secretary or deputy to accompany the commissioners, perform all clerical work, and prepare their report under the advice, supervision, and direction of the attorney for the district.

headings.title: Commissioners' service reports, court-set pay, and expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Directs commissioners to report days employed and actual expenses to the board of supervisors, providing daily pay in an amount set by the court plus necessary expenses.

headings.title: Filing exceptions, summary hearing, and report confirmation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12338; prior revisions 1929–1909). Permits the district or property owners to file exceptions within 10 days after last publication under the preceding section, requires summary determination, and directs approval and confirmation of the modified report if estimated improvement cost is less than assessed benefits.

headings.title: Referring report back to commissioners and second exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Authorizes the court before final confirmation to refer the report back to commissioners with or without instructions, requires section 242.270 notice upon refiling, and sets a 10-day deadline and summary hearing for exceptions to the second report.

headings.title: Exception costs and condemnation of needed property
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs the court to adjudge and apportion exception costs and condemn needed property or construction materials inside or outside the district following telegraph, telephone, and railroad right-of-way appropriation procedure.

headings.title: Transmitting and recording confirmed decree and report
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Directs the circuit clerk to send a certified decree and confirmed/amended report to the board secretary, who must transmit certified copies of the decree and county-specific report portions to each affected county recorder for permanent recording ($1 fee).

headings.title: Appeals and scope of reviewable questions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Permits any person to appeal the court judgment, limiting reviewable issues to whether just compensation was allowed for appropriated property and whether proper damages were allowed for prejudicially affected property.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (5 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12338; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and all five subsection fingerprints. Checked 10-day exceptions after prior-section publication, summary determination, and conditional confirmation where estimated cost is less than assessed benefits in (1), pre-confirmation referral back to commissioners, section 242.270 notice, and second 10-day exceptions in (2), cost apportionment and right-of-way-style condemnation in (3), clerk-to-secretary-to-county-recorder certified transmission ($1 fee) in (4), and appeals limited to just compensation and proper damages in (5). Retained all five titles as accurate.

headings.title: Authority and limits for amending district decrees
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12366, A. 1949 S.B. 1082; prior revision 1929 § 10785). Permits the court at any time to amend district organization, confirmation, boundary, reorganization, or procedural decrees to correct/add owner names, land descriptions, or other necessary items, qualified against impairing district obligations or relieving obligation security.

headings.title: Amendment petition, service of notice, and objection deadline
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires a board petition setting out proposed changes, owner names, and land descriptions, specifies service on non-party owners under section 506.150 (residents), section 506.160(6) or section 242.030 publication (nonresidents), or section 242.030 publication (unknown owners), and sets a 15-day objection period after publication or personal service.

headings.title: Summary hearing, multiple amendments, and court discretion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs speedy summary hearing of the petition and objections, permits combining any number of amendments or corrections in one petition, and authorizes allowing or rejecting them as just and right.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12366, A. 1949 S.B. 1082; prior revision 1929 § 10785); verified source identity and all three subsection fingerprints. Checked broad decree-amendment authority qualified against impairing obligations or relieving security in (1), board petition, service on non-party owners under sections 506.150, 506.160(6), and 242.030, and 15-day objection deadline in (2), and speedy summary hearing, multiple amendments in one petition, and court discretion in (3). Retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Petition to amend reclamation plan and request commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12367, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, effective 1-2-79; prior revision 1929 § 10786). Allows the board of a district organized under sections 242.010 to 242.690 to petition the organizing court clerk to amend the plan for reclamation, setting out changes and requesting three commissioners if prior appraisals and assessments have already been made.

headings.title: Notice form and two-week publication requirements
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including the statutory notice form table, its continuation paragraph, and notes. Directs the circuit clerk to notify property owners by newspaper publication, provides a sufficient notice form, and specifies in the post-table continuation paragraph once-weekly insertion for two consecutive weeks in each county containing district lands.

headings.title: Objections, summary hearing, ruling, and certified copy
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Gives affected property owners 10 days after last publication to file objections, directs summary hearing resulting in dismissal or whole/partial decree of amendment, and requires the circuit clerk to furnish a certified copy to the board secretary for preservation.

headings.title: Commissioners for amended plan and unpaid-benefit limits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Permits appointing three section 242.240-qualified commissioners at the same session to assess benefits and damages from the amended plan under original-report procedures, subject to the proviso that when bonds or negotiable debt are outstanding, new assessments cannot reduce unpaid assessed benefits by more than 10% or below 125% of principal.

headings.title: Payment before entry, five-year abatement, and title vesting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12353; prior revisions 1929 § 10772, 1919 § 4405). Bars entering or appropriating land under sections 242.010 to 242.690 until awarded prices are paid to owners or the circuit clerk, abates unpaid taking proceedings at district cost after five years from filing commissioners' reports, and vests title, use, possession, and disposition in the district upon payment.

headings.title: Cash payment of awards and assessing remaining tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires cash payment of land-acquisition prices and court-confirmed damages to the owner or court clerk, while providing that the untaken portion of any tract or property is assessed for benefits under sections 242.010 to 242.690.

Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Direct construction authority, labor, and equipment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12339, A.L. 1976 S.B. 915; prior revisions 1929–1909). Empowers the board to construct, excavate, and complete reclamation works directly by employing labor and teams, purchasing and operating machinery, or using other more efficient means.

headings.title: Bidding, contractor bonds, and written construction contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Grants discretion to let work contracts whole or in sections, requiring advertising and award to the lowest and best bidder, an approved performance bond, and a duplicate written contract prepared by the attorney for the district incorporating the chief engineer's plans and specifications and approved/signed before work begins.

headings.title: Chief engineer superintendence and state or federal aid
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Makes the chief engineer superintendent of works with at least annual reporting to the board, and authorizes the board to cooperate with Missouri or federal agencies willing to build plan works, accept grants/labor/work/materials, and provide required assurances.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12339, A.L. 1976 S.B. 915; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and all three subsection fingerprints. Refined reviewNote in (2) to specify 'attorney for the district'; retained all three titles as accurate.

headings.title: Enlarging or adding works for equal drainage and protection
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12350; prior revision 1929 § 10769). Authorizes the board, after plan filing and work progress and upon chief engineer recommendation, to enlarge existing improvements or build additional ditches, levees, canals, or works where plan improvements fail to give adjacent lands substantially equal drainage outlets or overflow protection as equally taxed district lands.

headings.title: Recording and filing description of additional works
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires filing a description of the necessary additional ditches and improvements with the board secretary, entering it on board records, and filing a certified copy with the organizing circuit clerk to make it part of the plan for reclamation.

headings.title: Paying for additional works and annexed-land exception
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs paying costs out of court-confirmed assessed benefits proportionally like original plan works, subject to the proviso barring levy against lands annexed after organization unless directly benefitted by the additional works.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (3 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12350; prior revision 1929 § 10769); verified source identity and all three subsection fingerprints. Checked chief-engineer-recommended enlargements or additional ditches/levees/canals for substantially equal drainage outlets and overflow protection among equally taxed lands in (1), recording with the board secretary and filing a certified copy with the circuit clerk in (2), and payment from confirmed assessed benefits subject to the proviso excluding post-organization annexed lands unless directly benefitted in (3). Revised (1) to 'Enlarging or adding works for equal drainage and protection' to cover overflow protection alongside drainage outlets; retained (2) and (3).

headings.title: Chief engineer plans and orders for bridges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12354, A.L. 1949 p. 260; prior revisions 1929–1909). Requires all bridges and bridge enlargements under sections 242.010 to 242.690 to be built and enlarged in compliance with plans, specifications, and orders made or approved by the district's chief engineer.

headings.title: Corporate bridges, notice, board letting, and cost recovery
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Covers delivering the board's bridge-necessity order to a corporation's agent or officer, treating untimely failure as refusal, board authority to let the work at corporate expense recoverable by suit, and requiring at least 20 days' actual notice of letting time and place to a summonable corporate agent or officer.

headings.title: Landowner bridges built at private expense
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Permits any owner of land inside or outside the district to construct a bridge across any drain, ditch, canal, or excavation at the owner's own expense in compliance with sections 242.010 to 242.690.

headings.title: Highway crossings, county-approved bridges, and road maintenance
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Authorizes constructing and maintaining plan ditches across public highways without condemnation or damages, requires building a county-commission-approved bridge within 10 days after excavation finishes, and makes the bridge part of the road maintained by the road authority.

headings.title: Twenty-year maintenance limit, reconstruction, and government exclusion
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Caps a district's maintenance/reconstruction obligation on highway bridges at 20 years from first construction, grants road authorities permissive ('if they desire') reconstruction authority for destroyed bridges, and excludes the state and political/civil subdivisions from 'corporation' in this section. Notes cite 1952 Swisher Inv. Co. (upholding 1949 amendment) and 1976 Hoskins v. Shelby Co. (confirming county court discretion not to replace a collapsed bridge).

headings.title: Connecting pre-existing ditches and watercourses during construction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12376; prior revisions 1929–1909). Directs that existing ditches, drainage systems, and watercourses in a district organized under sections 242.010 to 242.690 be connected into plan works during construction if necessary to drain district lands.

headings.title: Written consent required for post-completion connections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Prohibits connecting drains or drainage systems built after plan completion without prior written board consent specifying method, terms, and conditions and approved by the chief engineer, requiring strict adherence.

headings.title: Circuit court petition over refused or declined consent
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Allows landowners refused by the board or declining granted consent terms to petition the circuit court for a summary, final, and binding decision.

headings.title: Restrictions on connections from outside the district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Prohibits private or municipal entities or landowners from connecting drainage works or wholly in-district drains with ditches, cuts, fills, roadbeds, levees, or artificial drainage wholly outside district limits without board consent or as provided in this section.

headings.title: Appointment and at-will service of overseers
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12368; prior revisions 1929 § 10787, 1919 § 4417). Empowers the board of supervisors to appoint one or more overseers serving at the board's will to preserve works constructed under sections 242.010 to 242.690.

headings.title: Repair, reporting, high-water inspection, and emergency call-outs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Assigns overseers duties to maintain works in repair, clear obstructions inside or outside the district, report conditions, inspect levees during high water as directed, and—under archived emergency authority—call out able-bodied men over 16 and under 50 within the district to protect works.

headings.title: Misdemeanor penalties for refusal and daily work pay
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Describes the archived misdemeanor offense, arrest warrant and trial before an associate circuit judge, fine ($20–$100) and/or county jail (15–60 days) for refusing overseer-assigned emergency work, and $1.50 daily pay from district funds for performed work.

headings.title: Uniform per-acre organization tax levy and purposes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12333, A.L. 1959 H.B. 314, A.L. 2008 S.B. 939; prior revisions 1929–1909). Directs the board upon election and qualification to levy a uniform tax up to $8 per acre on district lands in the articles to pay organizing, survey, assessment, and pre-section 242.450 expenses.

headings.title: Applying organization tax to annexed lands
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires applying the same uniform organization tax to lands and property annexed under section 242.050 as soon as included in the district.

headings.title: Due date, delinquency, lien, surplus, and dissolution refunds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Makes the tax due upon assessment and delinquent after December 31, creates a lien collected like annual installments, directs surplus to the general fund for construction, and requires prorated refunds to paying landowners if dissolved under section 242.290.

headings.title: Levy on assessed benefits, emergencies, and apportionment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12340, A.L. 1977 S.B. 2; prior revisions 1929–1909). Note source discrepancy: the official Revisor catchline begins 'Organization of commissioners — duties of secretary of board of supervisors' (repeating 242.250), whereas subsection 1 requires levying a tax on assessed benefits after section 242.280 filing to pay plan completion costs plus 10% for emergencies, apportioned proportionally and not exceeding assessed benefits.

headings.title: New tax levy for replacing, repairing, or reconstructing works
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Authorizes the board, notwithstanding sections 242.280, 242.290, or chapter tax limits, after levying under 'paragraph 1' (archived internal phrasing) to levy a new proportional tax on assessed benefits when necessary to replace, repair, and reconstruct completed original-plan drainage works.

headings.title: Estimated bond interest in levies and cost comparisons
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires adding board-estimated accruing bond interest to levies under 'paragraph 1 or 2' (archived internal phrasing), while excluding such interest from construction costs when determining whether costs equal or exceed assessed benefits; title revised in review to cover both levy addition and the cost-comparison exclusion.

headings.title: Preparing and certifying the drainage tax record
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Directs the board secretary at district expense to compile all levied taxes in a well-bound, page-endorsed 'Drainage Tax Record' signed and certified by the president and secretary under seal as a permanent office record.

headings.title: Annual installment levy, due timing, and September 30 certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12341, A.L. 1953 p. 539, A.L. 2017 S.B. 112; prior revisions 1929–1909). Directs the board each year to levy the annual installment of section 242.450 taxes, collectible with state and county taxes, and certify it to county or township collectors by September 30 (note archived Sept. 1 dates retained in 242.490(1) and 242.590(1)).

headings.title: Tax certificate form and required tax book columns
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 including the statutory certificate form table, the continuation text, subdivisions (1) through (7), and notes. Prescribes a substantially sufficient certificate form referencing sections 242.450, 242.460, and 242.490, followed by a seven-column schedule for owners, descriptions, installment tax, maintenance tax, and collector payment/date/payer entries.

headings.title: Totaling tax columns and binding the drainage tax book
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires accurately totaling annual installment and maintenance tax columns to match the certificate and preparing the certificate and table as a well-bound, page-endorsed 'Drainage Tax Book'.

headings.title: New or amended plans and section 242.260 assessments
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12374; prior revisions 1929–1909). Authorizes formulating new or amended plans for new or enlarged works when original plan works prove insufficient, with additional assessments under section 242.260 in proportion to increased benefits.

headings.title: Additional tax levy within assessed benefits cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Permits ('may') an additional levy if total section 242.450 taxes are insufficient for original or additional works under this section, subject to the proviso that total levies not exceed total assessed benefits.

headings.title: Bond authorization, amount cap, interest, maturity, and execution
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12369; prior revisions 1929–1909; cross-references 108.180–108.230 and 108.140–108.160). Permits issuing bonds up to 90% of section 242.450 taxes in at least $100 denominations, up to 6% semiannual interest, annual maturities within 20 years commencing within 5 years, named bank/trust payment office, and officer execution under seal.

headings.title: Delivery to treasurer, minimum sale price, and payment source
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs delivering executed bonds to the treasurer for sale as needed by the board at not less than 95 cents on the dollar plus accrued interest, showing their purpose on their face and payable from levied taxes.

headings.title: Separate bond fund, past-due interest, and payment expenses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires setting aside drainage tax proceeds in a dedicated bond principal/interest fund, sets 6% interest on unpaid matured bonds/coupons from delinquent tax penalties/interest or available funds, and directs paying bond-payment expenses and bank compensation from administration funds.

headings.title: Annual levy provision, additional levies, and bond security
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires accounting for maturing bonds and interest in annual levies, making additional benefit levies if original section 242.450 proceeds fall short, and bars any tax levy that impairs bond security or payment funds.

headings.title: Treasurer's bond for bond-sale proceeds and custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires the treasurer upon receiving bonds to execute an approved surety bond to the board president covering sale proceeds, authorized deliveries, and returning cancelled unsold bonds, kept in the president's custody and produced for inspection or evidence when requested.

headings.title: Reporting bond sales, payment warrants, and remitting funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and notes. Requires prompt reporting of bond sales, board issuance of section 242.210-form warrants specifying bonds and interest to pay, and the treasurer placing funds and bank compensation at the payment place.

headings.title: Successor treasurer compliance before receiving bonds or proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and notes. Bars any successor treasurer from receiving bonds or bond proceeds until complying with all preceding requirements applicable to the predecessor.

headings.title: Corporate surety option and temporary bank depositary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 8 and notes. Permits furnishing the treasurer's bond through an approved surety/bonding company if directed by the board, plus the proviso allowing board resolution designating a bank or depositary as temporary treasurer to hold and disburse bond-sale funds.

headings.title: Restricted use of bond sale proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 9 and cross-reference notes (108.180–108.230, 108.140–108.160). Limits bond sale proceeds exclusively to paying drainage works and improvements and legally authorized costs, expenses, fees, and salaries.

headings.title: Additional bond cap and repair or reconstruction uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1977 S.B. 2). Permits issuing additional bonds up to 90% of new taxes levied under 'paragraph 2 of section 242.450', restricting proceeds solely to replacing, repairing, and reconstructing completed original-plan works.

headings.title: Two-thirds acreage approval and voting procedures
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Conditions issuance of additional bonds on approval at a called meeting by owners of two-thirds of assessed-benefit acreage, voting under sections 242.150 and 242.160.

headings.title: Form of meeting notice for additional bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including the statutory notice form table ('NOTICE OF MEETING OF ______ DRAINAGE DISTRICT') and notes. headings.title: Newspaper publication of meeting notice
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires the secretary to publish the meeting notice once weekly for two consecutive weeks in each county containing district lands, with last insertion at least 10 days before the meeting.

headings.title: Governing issuance procedures under section 242.480
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Incorporates section 242.480 to govern all other aspects of issuing the additional bonds.

headings.title: Maintenance tax authorization, twenty-percent cap, and certification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12370, A.L. 1990 S.B. 777; prior revisions 1929 § 10789, 1919 § 4419). Permits levying a 'maintenance tax' on or before September 1 annually after completion of improvements (apportioned on net original or readjusted benefits, capped at 20% per year) and requires certifying it in a separate column alongside the annual installment tax.

headings.title: Collection, combining contiguous tracts, and error corrections
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Sets collector collection, return, compensation, and penalty duties (retaining archived phrase 'as is provided in this section' without alteration), permits board resolution after total-tax installments end to combine contiguous commonly owned tracts using deed-record names and conformed section 242.460 certificates at the same aggregate tax, and prevents errors from invalidating the tax or lien while allowing correction by board resolution.

headings.title: Readjustment petition, notice form, hearing, and court order
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including the statutory notice form table, post-table continuation paragraph, and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12371, A.L. 1977 S.B. 2, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, A.L. 1985 H.B. 378, A.L. 1990 S.B. 777, A.L. 2008 S.B. 939; prior revisions 1929 § 10709, 1919 § 4420). headings.title: Commissioners, assessment scope, tax caps, frequency, and recording
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. headings.title: Tax levy on readjusted benefits and total-benefit cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1977 S.B. 2). Directs the board, if deemed necessary, to levy a proportional tax on readjusted assessed benefits for section 242.230 supplemental plan works plus 10% for emergencies, subject to the proviso that new plus unpaid prior levies not exceed total readjusted benefits.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires levying the readjusted-benefit tax in the manner provided in sections 242.450 and 242.460.

headings.title: Bond cap under section 242.502 and permitted uses
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1977 S.B. 2). headings.title: Issuance procedures under section 242.480
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires issuing bonds pursuant to and in accordance with section 242.480.

headings.title: New tax and bond authority for supplemental works
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1977 S.B. 2). Authorizes the board, notwithstanding sections 242.280, 242.290, or chapter tax limits, after a section 242.502 levy to levy a new proportional tax on readjusted benefits (under sections 242.450 and 242.460) and, if necessary, issue additional bonds to replace, repair, and reconstruct completed supplemental-plan works.

headings.title: Issuance procedures and cap for additional bonds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires issuing the 'paragraph 1' (archived internal phrasing) additional bonds under sections 242.480 and 242.485, subject to the proviso capping them at 90% of new taxes levied under this section.

headings.title: Borrowing cap, three-fifths election approval, and proxy voting
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12387; prior revisions 1929–1909). Applies to level-assessment districts (organized prior to April 8, 1905 per section 242.510/heading), permitting borrowing up to $6 per acre principal for works, surveys, or rights-of-way with consent of owners of at least three-fifths of district lands at a noticed election, and allows written proxy voting at that election or any landowner election.

headings.title: Loan terms, bond sale floor, and repayment tax cap
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Caps loan term at 20 years and semiannual interest at 6%, sets a 90-cents-on-the-dollar net bond sale floor, and requires an annual levy up to 50 cents per acre to pay maturing principal and interest.

headings.title: County collector duties, tax book authority, and divided tracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12342; prior revisions 1929–1909). Directs county collectors in districts under sections 242.010 to 242.690 to receive the drainage tax book as collection warrant, collect drainage taxes with state and county taxes, and accept and receipt taxes on portions of divided or transferred tracts.

headings.title: Annual return of tax books, affidavit, and remitting funds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires county collectors to return drainage tax books annually to the board secretary verified by affidavit and remit and account for collected funds to the district treasurer when paying state and county taxes.

headings.title: Certifying and collecting the drainage back tax book
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs the board secretary within 10 days after collector return to prepare, certify, and deliver a drainage back tax book of delinquent property to the collector (taking a receipt) for collection like current drainage taxes.

headings.title: Collector's bond, board approval, and secretary custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires each county collector before receiving the tax book to execute an approved two-surety bond to the board in the probable annual installment amount, deposited with the secretary for custody and lawful inspection or evidentiary use.

headings.title: Township tax books in chapter 65 counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12377, A.L. 2005 H.B. 58 merged with S.B. 210; prior revisions 1929 § 10796, 1919 § 4426). In counties under chapter 65, requires extending sections 242.010 to 242.690 drainage taxes on separate township books certified to the collector-treasurer like county collectors.

headings.title: Current tax collection, bond, return, and liabilities
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs the collector-treasurer to collect township drainage taxes with state and county taxes under the same bond, authority, compensation, remittance to the board secretary, penalties, liabilities, and sworn-return duties as county collectors.

headings.title: Delinquent tax certification and collection in chapter 65 counties
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Directs certifying delinquent drainage taxes to the county collector-treasurer of delinquent taxes, who collects and remits them to the district treasurer under the same procedures, bond, compensation, penalties, and liabilities as non-chapter 65 county collectors.

headings.title: Prima facie evidence, lien enforcement, and delinquent tax suits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Makes township tax books and collector returns prima facie evidence in all courts and requires enforcing liens and instituting delinquent tax suits by the drainage district on certified tax bills from the county collector-treasurer of delinquent taxes.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (4 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12377, A.L. 2005 H.B. 58 merged with S.B. 210; prior revisions 1929–1919); verified source identity and all four subsection fingerprints. Retained all four titles as accurate.

headings.title: Early full payment of construction tax without interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12378; prior revisions 1929 § 10797, 1919 § 4427). Grants property owners assessed for construction under sections 242.010 to 242.690 the privilege to pay the full tax assessment less added interest to the board treasurer on or before a board-fixed date.

headings.title: Recording paid-in-full satisfaction in district and county records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs the board secretary upon full payment to mark 'paid in full' on the drainage tax record to satisfy the assessment and enter the same notation in the section 242.590 recorder certificate table.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12378; prior revisions 1929–1919); verified source identity and both subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Drainage tax lien priority and certificate form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including the statutory lien certificate form table and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12345; prior revisions 1929–1909). Makes sections 242.010 to 242.690 drainage taxes, default penalties, collection costs, and court-fixed attorney's fee a lien from recorder certificate filing subordinate only to state general, county, school, and road tax liens, and prescribes the certificate form (note archived form still recites September 1 certification rather than section 242.460(1)'s September 30).

headings.title: Binding, filing, and fee for drainage tax record
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires the board secretary at district expense to prepare the certificate and tables in a well-bound 'Drainage Tax Record' filed as a permanent record with each affected county recorder for a one-dollar fee.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections, including the embedded lien certificate form table in (1)) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12345; prior revisions 1929–1909); verified source identity and both subsection fingerprints. headings.title: Drainage tax book as prima facie evidence
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12346; prior revisions 1929–1909). Declares the collector-returned drainage tax book prima facie evidence in all courts of all matters therein contained.

headings.title: Delinquent tax lien suits, timing, venue, and procedure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and case annotations (four 1955 and 1958 Fort Osage Drainage Dist. cases on de facto officers, county highway tax recovery, and district standing). Requires enforcing tax liens by circuit court action on certified delinquent tax bills within six months after December 31 regardless of claim amount, filed by the district's attorney in the property's county (or any county of a multicounty tract) following general real estate tax lien practice.

headings.title: Sheriff's sales, deeds, evidence, and subsequent tax liens
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Requires sheriff sales under general revenue law, equates probative force of sheriff's deeds, abbreviations, and the drainage tax book to general state tax lien actions, and keeps sale titles subject to subsequent annual drainage tax installment liens.

headings.title: Judgment costs, attorney's fees, and sale proceeds
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes (including 1958 Fort Osage Drainage Dist. v. Foley on attorney fees). Requires including suit costs and a court-fixed reasonable attorney's fee in delinquent tax judgments and paying sale proceeds immediately to the district treasurer to be accounted for like drainage taxes.

headings.title: Required defendants in delinquent assessment suits
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1941 p. 351 § 1). Requires any Missouri drainage or levee district suing to collect delinquent annual assessments to name the last record land owner(s) and join trustees and beneficiaries of recorded deeds of trust, mortgages, or vendors' liens, with no other parties necessary except as provided.

headings.title: Recording suit notice, fee, and notice effect
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires the district's attorney on suit-filing day to file a verified tabulated notice with the county recorder ($1 fee, recorded in a well-bound book), constituting due and proper notice to all non-required parties holding unrecorded conveyances or note assignments or acquiring interests afterward; title revised in review from 'binding effect' to 'notice effect' to preserve distinction from subsection 3's judgment-binding rule.

headings.title: Intervention duty for unrecorded or subsequent interest holders
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Grants unrecorded or post-notice interest holders and secured-note assignees a right and duty to intervene as defendants by the first day of the summons return term, binds non-intervenors to judgment, and passes all parties' interests at execution sale unless assessments are previously paid.

headings.title: District bidding at tax sales and disposing of acquired land
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12347; prior revision 1929 § 10766; cross-reference 140.380). Authorizes the board to bid up to total taxes, interest, costs, and penalties when no full bid is made at a delinquent sale, take a sheriff's deed if highest bidder, and hold, dispose of, and convey the land on terms in the district's best interest.

headings.title: Board-sold property subject to subsequent drainage taxes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Provides that purchasers of land or other property sold by the board of supervisors take the property subject to all subsequently due drainage taxes like other district property; title revised in review to avoid implying personal liability.

headings.title: Paying general taxes and one-year redemption after foreclosure
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and cross-reference note (140.380). Authorizes the board to pay general state, county, school, and road taxes to protect its lien, and allows redeeming property within one year after a general tax foreclosure sale to which the district was not made a party by paying up to accrued taxes, penalties, and costs.

headings.title: Bar on change of venue except judicial disqualification
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12358, A.L. 1978 H.B. 1634, effective 1-2-79; prior revisions 1929 § 10777, 1919 § 4410). Prohibits any change of venue in proceedings under sections 242.010 to 242.690 except where the filing court's judge is disqualified for civil venue statutory reasons.

headings.title: Assigning substitute judge and duration of jurisdiction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires a disqualified judge, or one charged with disqualification by an interested person, to have another judge transferred or assigned as in civil cases, whose jurisdiction lasts only until the regular circuit judge's disqualification is removed.

headings.title: Preserving prior rights, pending proceedings, and contracts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12389; prior revisions 1929 § 10808, 1919 § 4438). Historical saving clause ensuring repeal of RSMo 1909 Ch. 41 Art. 1 and the 1911 amendatory act does not impair prior drainage district rights, powers, remedies, or liens, pending state or federal court proceedings, or existing contracts and obligations.

headings.title: Electing enforcement procedures and liberal remedial construction
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Permits drainage districts to elect enforcement of existing rights, powers, liens, and remedies under prior law or sections 242.010 to 242.690 if applicable, and declares those sections remedial and liberally construed.

entries.reviewSummary: Independently read the complete archived version (2 subsections) and source notes (RSMo 1939 § 12389; prior revisions 1929–1919); verified source identity and both subsection fingerprints. Retained both titles as accurate.

headings.title: Major district acceptance or rejection and court filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (L. 1961 p. 444 §§ 3 to 6). Requires the major district board within 90 days after service of a minor district's annexation petition under sections 242.692 to 242.699 to order acceptance or rejection and requires its secretary to file a certified copy with the circuit clerk within 20 days.

headings.title: Published annexation notice, combined assessments, and objection right
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs four consecutive weekly newspaper publications upon acceptance, allows collective description of minor-district owners/property, sets required notice disclosures (assumption of liabilities, adopted and overlap-combined benefit assessments, termination of minor district), and grants minor-district assessed owners an objection right—retaining exact archived wording 'within fifteen days but not after the last publication of notice' without silent alteration.

headings.title: Objection scope, speedy hearing, and annexation decree
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Limits objections to denying petition statements, requires setting hearing within 15 days after the filing period expires for speedy determination at a regular, adjourned, or special term, and directs entering an annexation judgment and decree under sections 242.692 to 242.699 if findings are true.

headings.title: Serving decree, transferring assets, and terminating minor district
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires serving a certified decree on a minor-district officer, delivering books, records, and supplies to the major district secretary, transferring moneys and property from the minor district treasurer to the major district treasurer against receipt, and thereby terminating the minor district's existence.

headings.title: Mine drainage survey, concentrating plant plans, and adoption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12392). Directs a mine drainage district's section 242.220 chief engineer to survey surface, underground, and adjacent mineralized lands and submit maps, profiles, dewatering plans, custom concentrating plant designs, and ore estimates for board adoption as the section 242.230 plan for reclamation.

headings.title: Tax and charge resolution and two-week notice publication
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Directs the board upon plan adoption to adopt a resolution providing for taxes and charges (including section 242.740 increases) and publish the resolution once weekly for two consecutive weeks in each district county.

headings.title: Filing landowner exceptions to tax levies or charges
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Allows owners of land within the mine drainage district or benefitted adjacent land to file exceptions to tax levies or charges with the board secretary within 10 days after last notice publication.

headings.title: Board hearing and circuit court review of exceptions
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Requires the board to hear and determine exceptions within 5 days, and allows a dissatisfied landowner to petition the organizing circuit court for hearing and determination under section 242.280.

headings.title: Chief engineer drainage records and annual written reports
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and notes. Requires the chief engineer to keep complete records of district drainage, affected lands, and concentrating plant operations, filing written reports when requested by the board and at least once yearly.

headings.title: Pumping royalty tax, milling charge, and revenue sufficiency
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12393). Directs the board's resolution to levy a pumping tax royalty on mineral concentrates (capped at 2% of gross sale value) and a per-ton milling tax/charge for crushing and cleaning ores, fixed together to cover bond interest, maturing bonds, operating expenses, and maintenance/depreciation/contingency reserves.

headings.title: Bank deposits, collateral security, and restricted fund use
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Requires depositing tax and charge receipts in a solvent bank or trust company secured by collateral or otherwise as board-directed, and restricts their use exclusively to authorized purposes.

headings.title: Paramount lien, holding possession, and selling ores or concentrates
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes. Creates a first and paramount lien on mined ores, minerals, and concentrates and authorizes the board to retain possession until paid or sell them on the open market and remit the balance after deducting taxes and charges.

headings.title: Contracts securing continuous operations and tax payment
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and notes. Authorizes the board to contract with affected landowners, lessees, or other interested persons using provisions needed to secure continuous mine and concentrating-plant operation and prompt tax/charge payment under sections 242.700 to 242.750.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and notes (RSMo 1939 § 12394). headings.title: Pledging or mortgaging district property and net revenues
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and notes. Authorizes the board to pledge, mortgage, or convey district real and personal property and tax/charge proceeds remaining after operating expenses and maintenance/depreciation/contingency reserves to secure bonds and interest.

headings.title: State auditor registration and section 242.480 or federal sales
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and notes.
